column2: There was formerly one fire; by him the Treta (three fires) was set going. Pururavas, devoted to yoga, went to the world of the Gandharvas.
Ayu, Dridhayu, Ashvayu, Dhanayu, Dhritiman, Vasu, Divijata and Shatayu — Urvashi bore these kings.
Ayu's son was Nahusha; Vriddhasharma, Raji, Darbha, Vipapma; Raji had a hundred sons of the Panchagni (line).
They were famed as Rajeyas; Raji, whose boon was given by Vishnu, killed demons in the battle of gods and demons, begged by the gods;
having given Indra sonship, the departed gave him the kingdom and went to heaven. Raji's sons took away Indra's kingdom, ill-minded;
by the rule of planet-pacification and the rest the teacher gave it to Indra; having bewildered Raji's sons, they remained following their own duty.
Nahusha's seven sons: Yati, Yayati the best, Udbhava and Panchaka, Sharyati, Meghapalaka;
Yati, even in boyhood, meditating on Vishnu, went to Hari. Devayani, Indra's (Shukra's) daughter, then became Yayati's wife;
Sharmishtha, born of Vrishaparva, was Yayati's: five sons of his. Devayani bore Yadu and Turvasu;
Sharmishtha daughter of Vrishaparva bore Druhyu, Anu and Puru. Yadu and Puru were the increasers of their line.
From Titikshu Marutta; from him Kambalabarhisha; fifty from Rukmakavacha; Rukmeshu, Prithurukmaka;
Havis, Jyamagha the sin-destroyer; Jyamagha was ruled by a wife. On Shaibya by Jyamagha was Vidarbha; his Kaushika;
Lomapada, Kratha; from Shreshtha Kriti; from Lomapada...; Chidi the son of Kaushika; from him the Chaidya kings are remembered.
From Kratha, the sons of Vidarbha; Kunti, and of Kunti, Dhrishtaka; of Dhrishta Nidhriti; his Udarka named Vidura-ratha;
Dasharha's son Vyoma; from Vyoma Jimuta is said; Jimuta's son Vikala; his son Bhimaratha;
from Bhimaratha Navaratha; then Dridharatha; from Dridharatha Shakuni, and from Shakuni Karambhaka;
from Karambha Devarata, and Devakshetra his son; from Devakshetra Madhu by name; from Madhu Dravarasa;
from Dravarasa Puruhuta; Jantu was his son; Guni the Yadava king; Jantu's son was Satvata;
from Satvata Bhajamana, Vrishni, Andhaka and Devavridha — four; their lines are famed.
Of Bhajamana: Bahya, Vrishti, Krimi and Nimi; from Devavridha Babhru; a verse about him is sung here:
As we hear his virtues from afar, so from near: Babhru is best of men, Devavridha equal to the gods.
Four sons of Babhru, kings devoted to Vasudeva: Kuhura, Bhajamana, Shini, Kambalabarhisha.
Kuhura's son Dhrishnu; Dhrishnu's son Dhriti; from Dhriti Kapotaroma; his son Tittiri;
Tittiri's son Nara, his Chandanadundubhi; Punarvasu his son; Ahuka and the son of Ahuki;
from Ahuka Devaka was born; then Ugrasena; Devavan and Upadeva are remembered as Devaka's sons;
they had seven sisters, whom he gave to Vasudeva: Devaki, Shrutadevi, Mitradevi, Yashodhara,
Shridevi, Satyadevi and Surapi the seventh. Nine sons of Ugrasena, of whom Kamsa was the eldest:
Nyagrodha and Sunama, Kanka and Shanku the king, Sutanu, Rashtrapala, Yuddhamushti, Sumushtika.
Bhajamana's son was Viduratha, chief of charioteers; Rajadhideva and Shura were sons of Viduratha;
Rajadhideva's two sons: Shonashva and Shvetavahana; Shonashva's five sons Shami, Shatrujit and others;
Shami's son Pratikshetra; of Pratikshetra Bhoja; Bhoja's son Hridika; Hridika's ten sons:
Kritavarma, Shatadhanva, Devarha, Bhishana and others; from Devarha Kambalabarhis; from him Asamaujas;
Sudamshtra and Suvasa; Dhrishta was of Asamaujas. Gandhari and Madri were Dhrishta's two wives;
Sumitra was born of Gandhari; Madri bore Yudhajit. Anamitra, Shini from Dhrishta; then indeed Devamidhusha;
Anamitra's son Nighna; Nighna's Prasenaka. Satrajit and Prasena; the Syamantaka jewel (from the Sun);
Prasena, having obtained it, went in the forest and a lion killed him and took the jewel; the lion was killed by Jambavan; Jambavan was defeated by Hari;
from him, having obtained the jewel and Jambavati, he went to the city of Dvaraka. He gave it to Satrajit; Shatadhanva killed him.
Having killed Shatadhanva, Krishna, taking the jewel and winning fame, in front of Balarama and the chief Yadavas had Akrura offer the jewel.
Leaving the false accusation against Krishna, one who recites this goes to heaven. Satyabhama, Satrajit's daughter, was Hari's beloved.
From Anamitra Shini was born; Satyaka was Shini's son; from Satyaka Satyaki was born; from Yuyudhana Dhuni;
Dhuni's son Yugandhara; Svahya was Yudhajit's; Rishabha and Kshetraka his; from Rishabha Svaphalka;
Svaphalka's son Akrura; from Akrura Sudhanvaka; from Shura Vasudeva and the rest; Pritha became Pandu's beloved.
From Dharma, Yudhishthira of Pandu; from Vayu on Kunti, Vrikodara; from Indra, Dhananjaya; on Madri Nakula and Sahadeva;
from Vasudeva on Rohini, Rama, Sarana and Durgama; from Vasudeva on Devaki first was born Susenaka;
Kirtiman, Bhadrasena, Jarukhya, Vishnudasaka and Bhadradeha — Kamsa killed these six embryos.
Then Bala, then Krishna, Subhadra of kind speech; Charudeshna, Samba and others were Krishna's sons by Jambavati.
Having become foam of water in the battle of gods and demons, he carried off Vritra the god-seizer; Vishnu protected the gods' dharma.
Having conquered Shalva and other demons, Hari as Parashurama protected the gods and others, killing wicked Kshatriyas.
Having removed from Maheshvara the Halahala poison, the demon, Madhusudana destroyed the gods' fear.
In the battle of gods and demons the demon Kolahala was conquered; all the gods were protected by Vishnu through maintaining dharma.
Kings, princes, sages, deities — Hari; what has been told and what not told are these avatars of Hari.
From Sabhanara Kalanala; from Kalanala Srinjaya; Purunjaya from Srinjaya; his son Janamejaya;
his son Mahashala; his son was Mahamanas; from him Ushinara, Brahmin, and Nriga on Nriga's wife; then Nriga;
on Nara's wife Nara; and Krimi; Krimi's son. On Dasha Suvrata was born; on Drishadvati Shibi likewise;
Shibi's four sons: Prithudarbha, Viraka, Kaikeya, Bhadraka; by their names the auspicious countries.
Titikshu born of Ushinara, and of Titikshu Rushadratha; from Rushadratha Paila; from Paila Sutapas the son;
from him Mahayogi Bali; Anga, Vanga and Mukhya; Pundra, Kalinga, Baleya; Bali the yogi, endowed with strength.
From Anga Dadhivahana; from him king Divaratha; from Divaratha Dharmaratha; his son Chitraratha;
from Chitraratha Satyaratha and his son Lomapada; from Lomapada Chaturanga; his son Prithulaksha;
from Prithulaksha Champa; from Champa Haryanga; from Haryanga Bhadraratha and his son Brihatkarman;
from him Brihadbhanu; from Brihadbhanu Brihadatmavan; from him Jayadratha; from Jayadratha Brihadratha;
from Brihadratha Vishvajit; Karna from Vishvajit; Karna's Vrishasena; Prithusena his son. These are kings born of the Anga line; learn from me the line of Puru.
Suhotra's son Brihat; Brihat's three sons: Ajamidha, Dvimidha and the powerful Purumidha.
On Keshini Ajamidha begot the mighty Jahnu; from Jahnu Ajakashva; his son Balakashva;
Balakashva's Kushika; from Kushika Gadhi, Indraka; Gadhi's daughter Satyavati; Vishvamitra, best of charioteers;
Devarata and Katimukha — those were Vishvamitra's sons; Shunahshepha, Ashtaka and another were Ajamidha's sons;
on Nilini another, Shanti; from Sushanti Purujati; Purujati's Bahyashva; from Bahyashva five kings:
Mukula, Srinjaya, king Brihadishu, Yavinara and Krimila — famed as Panchalas.
Of Mukula the Maukulyas, twice-born with land; Chanchashva was born of Mukula; from Chanchashva a pair;
Divodasa and Ahalya; on Ahalya by Sharadvat, Shatananda; from Shatananda Satyadhriti and a pair thereafter;
Kripa and Kripi; from Divodasa Maitreya, then Somapa; from Srinjaya Panchadhanush, and his son Somadatta;
from Somadatta Sahadeva; from Sahadeva Somaka; from Somaka Jantu; of Jantu son Prishata;
from Prishata Drupada; from him Dhrishtadyumna and his son Dhrishtaketu; on Dhumini Riksha was born of Ajamidha;
from Riksha Samvarana; then Kuru from Samvarana, who moving away from Prayaga made Kurukshetra.
From Kuru Sudhanva, Sudhanus, Parikshit and Arimejaya; from Sudhanva Suhotra; from Suhotra Chyavana was born.
